clue.text: Four-letter word? Margaret taken aback, biting tongue at first

indicators.note: biting means one piece is held inside the jaws of the other
taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the name is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word tongue

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A woman named Margaret is startled and bites her tongue at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a tetragram is literally a word of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is a word or name consisting of exactly four characters, most famously the Hebrew name of God.

clue.text: Hitch in part of south Umbria

indicators.note: in part of tells us the answer sits inside a stretch of the words south Umbria

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A snag encountered while travelling through a region of southern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitch looks like a noun meaning a snag, but here it is the verb for hitch-hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a lift is to hitch-hike, so the verb means hitch in the travelling sense.

clue.text: First run out in international will

parts.note: a Test is an international match, especially in cricket
drive here means determination or willpower

explanation.surface: A batsman is run out first in an international cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out reads as cricket dismissal, but the definition means a first trial outing of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A test drive is a trial outing in a car before buying it, the first time a buyer takes it on the road.

clue.text: Scathing, series probing a hospital department

indicators.note: something probing pokes into another thing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a string is a series of things in a row

explanation.surface: A run of investigations into a hospital department proves severely critical.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is sharp and severe, a figurative synonym for harsh, cutting remarks.

clue.text: Raw fish delicacy and bap, followed by sponge

indicators.note: followed by places the second item straight after the first in the answer

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
to mop is to wipe up with a sponge or cloth; a mop is a sponge on a stick

explanation.surface: A lunch of pickled fish and a bread bun, with a sponge cake for afters.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a fillet of herring pickled in vinegar and rolled up, eaten uncooked as a delicacy.

clue.text: Small farm in Scotland belonging to me, fictional detective's brother

parts.note: my is the possessive for something belonging to me
a croft is a small tenant farm in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A smallholding in the Highlands that I own, linked to a sleuth's sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mycroft Holmes is the elder brother of Sherlock Holmes in Conan Doyle's stories.

clue.text: Leave Adriatic port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for depart quickly
second meaning: the Croatian city on the Adriatic coast

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like setting sail from a harbour; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is informal for going away, and Split is a major Croatian seaport on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Go crazy if upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word over, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a person may lose their mind if distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the noun here, as in have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab at something is an attempt, just as a go at it is a try.

clue.text: Learning about current in French river

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for learning wraps the current

parts.note: lore is accumulated knowledge or learning
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Studying the flow of water in a river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Reference book he's taken into house

indicators.note: taken into means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: Taurus is one of the twelve astrological houses of the zodiac
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man's dictionary has been brought into a home.
explanation.walkthrough: House is an astrological house, a sign of the zodiac, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference work listing synonyms, consulted like a dictionary.

clue.text: Winning group's surprise result

parts.note: up means ahead, as in two goals up
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A victorious team achieves an unexpected win.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is an unexpected victory by an underdog.

clue.text: New cultivar produced by European could be profitable

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of cultivar

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly bred plant variety from a European grower may earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: A cultivar is a cultivated plant variety; the word supplies the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means producing a great deal of money or gain, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Chap, slight, crossing second highest part of Cornwall

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow

indicators.note: crossing means one word straddles the other, so the short word sits within

parts.note: minor means slight or small
a mo is a moment, an informal second

explanation.surface: A slim man walks over the second-highest ground in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Second highest looks like one phrase; second is the wordplay, and highest part begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodmin Moor is a granite upland whose summit, Brown Willy, is the highest point in the county of Cornwall.

clue.text: Greek character after fine cheese

indicators.note: after places the Greek letter behind the abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person follows a delicate cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white brined cheese from Greece, made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Great hotel breaks with everything included

indicators.note: breaks suggests the words being smashed and their letters rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holidays at a grand hotel come all-inclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaks reads as holidays, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means in total, taking every part into account.

clue.text: Raise then call after foremost of bids

indicators.note: after puts the phone phrase behind the single letter
foremost of picks just the leading letter of the word bids

parts.note: only its first letter is taken
to ring up is to telephone someone

explanation.surface: At an auction someone raises the stakes and then shouts after the opening bids.
explanation.walkthrough: Raise and call sound like poker betting, but raise means rear a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to rear or raise it.

clue.text: Restless bovine brought in by southern miners

indicators.note: brought in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the word by

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: restless suggests the letters of bovine moving about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fidgety cow is led in by miners from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevin Boys were young British men conscripted to work in coal mines during the Second World War, named after minister Ernest Bevin.

clue.text: Old communications satellite rattles badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the word rattles being put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageing satellite makes a lot of clattering noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar, launched in 1962, was the first satellite to relay live television across the Atlantic.

clue.text: All of the footballers, say, in line on pitch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the total of two eleven-a-side teams on the field
second meaning: the line 22 metres from the try line on a rugby field

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a team lining up; the second sense is the rugby line, called the 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Two teams of eleven make twenty-two players, and a rugby pitch has a marked twenty-two metre line.

clue.text: Drive round active volcano in Asian country

indicators.note: round means the word for drive goes around the volcano

parts.note: vim means energy or drive
Etna in Sicily is a famously active volcano

explanation.surface: A road trip circles a smoking volcano in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a nation in Southeast Asia bordering China, Laos and Cambodia.

clue.text: Raised stuff concerning one Italian inventor

indicators.note: raised in a down clue lifts the word, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Raised material relating to an inventor from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian pioneer of long-distance radio transmission.

clue.text: Factory sirens upsetting to horse

indicators.note: upsetting suggests knocking the letters over and rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Loud factory alarms frighten a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooters are sirens or whistles, such as those that sounded shift changes at factories.

clue.text: Artist's animal painting, horse's head

parts.note: a hog is a pig
painting is a form of art

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word horse's

parts.note: only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A painter's animal picture shows a horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an eighteenth-century English painter and satirical engraver.

clue.text: Having nothing on tap, not good

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out of the word

parts.note: a nudge is a gentle tap or push

explanation.surface: A spare evening with nothing planned, and the plumbing is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing on reads as free time and on tap as available; the definition means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nude is naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Live adequately under daughter's roof

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the second piece below the first
the roof of a word in a down clue is its top letter, here of daughter's

parts.note: only its top letter is taken, the abbreviation for daughter
well means satisfactorily or adequately

explanation.surface: Getting by comfortably while lodging in a daughter's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make one's home there.

clue.text: Disorganised father having put on uniform is ignored

indicators.note: is ignored means the letter for uniform is dropped from the word

parts.note: augmented means added to or put on
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A messy dad has put on his uniform, but nobody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: Put on reads as dressing in uniform, but it means added to.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmented means broken into pieces, so lacking order or coherence.

clue.text: Tricked theologian about winning percentage at the end

indicators.note: about means the theologian's letters surround the rest

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
up means ahead or winning

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of the word percentage

parts.note: only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A theologian was misled about his success rate in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be duped is to be fooled or deceived by someone.

clue.text: Chief isle's surrounding another

indicators.note: surrounding means the island's name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
another isle, abbreviated to I

explanation.surface: One island encircles a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means principal or most important, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unfortunately agree, poor musical dramas may often be seen by one

definitions.text: musical dramas may often be seen by one

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the words going wrong and their letters being jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully concedes that sung stage works are often badly performed.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera-goer is a regular attender of operas, the sung dramatic works in question.

clue.text: Hot under the collar, ambassador with temperature on the rise

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
up means rising

explanation.surface: An envoy feels the heat as the temperature climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal style of an ambassador.

clue.text: Son by himself briefly in beauty parlour

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: alone means by oneself

explanation.surface: A boy goes on his own to a hairdresser's for a quick visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business offering hairdressing or beauty treatments.

clue.text: Is golf club accepting that female novelist?

indicators.note: accepting means the words for is and golf club take the pronoun between them

parts.note: taken as written
a wood is a golf club with a large head
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A question whether a golf club admits a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: That female reads as the novelist, but the novelist meant is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English-born novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.
